---
title: "Practice: Univariate Categorical Data Summaries"

# Introduction

In this practice, you will summarize one categorical variable at a time. For each dataset, make a table of counts and proportions, then use `barplot()` to display the categories in sorted order.

Use `table()` to count the categories, `prop.table()` to find proportions, and `sort(..., decreasing = TRUE)` to put the largest category first. You may save a sorted table as an object and use that object in `barplot()`.

# Question 1: How Do Students Get to Campus?

A class survey asked 24 students how they usually travel to campus. The responses are in the vector below.

```{r}
travel <- c(
  "Walk", "Car", "Walk", "Bus", "Car", "Walk",
  "Bike", "Car", "Walk", "Bus", "Car", "Walk",
  "Car", "Bike", "Walk", "Car", "Bus", "Walk",
  "Car", "Walk", "Bike", "Car", "Walk", "Bus"
)
```
